title: Near walls read as weathered stone or plaster, not flat paint
note: Near walls read as weathered stone or plaster with courses, grime and wear, not as flat painted colour.
intent: At eye height a wall is judged on its surface, and a single base colour on a standard material reads as painted card. Give the near walls a baked map from the project's material baker with three things in it: the structure (courses, panel joints, plank lines), a grime gradient darkening the bottom half metre and under the eaves, and a low-frequency blotch so no two square metres look the same. Add a roughness map so wet and worn areas differ, and a normal or bump map fine enough to catch the grazing light. Noise on its own is not texture — the judge names that separately as noise-as-texture.

check.ask: Do the nearest walls read as weathered stone or plaster with visible surface texture (courses, grime, wear), rather than flat painted colour?
check.note: The material read the taste judge kept naming as [primitive] / [noise-as-texture].

port: The facet that owns buildings bakes wall materials in the project's material baker and applies them by tag; the check is answered from eye:spawn.
